articles.title: SJAA EPHEMERIS
articles.summary: This document is titled "SJAA EPHEMERIS" and represents Volume 4, Number 3 of the official publication of the San Jose Astronomical Association. Published in March 1993, it serves as a regular bulletin for its members, likely containing information pertinent to the club's activities, observing opportunities, and astronomical events for that month.

articles.title: The Eye Piece
articles.summary: The article makes three key announcements: an urgent call for nominations for the annual Dr. Gregory award, a request from Ethan Cliffton for sketches of 10" or 12" compound telescopes and CCD cameras for a fixed shutter design, and the availability of MacEphem freeware thanks to Bill O'Shaughnessy. Members are encouraged to participate in the award nominations and contact Bill for software copies.

articles.title: Calendar
articles.summary: This document outlines a calendar of astronomy-related events for March, April, and May. It includes numerous star parties at various locations, monthly general meetings featuring guest speakers on topics like SETI and digital setting circles, and sessions for an astronomy class. Key events also include an Astronomy Day celebration and an SJAA auction and swap.

articles.title: Decisions, Decisions
articles.summary: The article announces several upcoming astronomy events for 1993, including the Texas Star Party, Riverside Telescope Makers Conference, and Universe '93, while also promoting a "Telescope Making with John Dobson" video. A significant portion details the new NASA FOSTER Program, an educational outreach initiative providing flight opportunities for Bay-Area science teachers on the Kuiper Airborne Observatory (KAO) to enrich science education.

articles.title: Observational Astronomy Class
articles.summary: The first observational astronomy class, led by Jack Petersen, was successfully held on January 30, 1993, at the Milpitas Library. Aimed at helping amateur astronomers find celestial objects, the class covered topics such as planetary motions, constellations (e.g., Ursa Major, Ursa Minor), and Messier objects. Many experienced attendees participated, enhancing their understanding of the night sky.

articles.title: DOUBLES
articles.summary: This document provides predictions and orbital data for a selection of double stars, compiled from British Astronomical Association handbooks (1986-1993). It serves as a guide for amateur astronomers, indicating which double stars are suitable tests for telescopes ranging from 3" to 30" aperture based on their changing separations and position angles. Specific notes detail the evolving visibility of several prominent pairs, highlighting their closing or widening over time.

articles.title: Doubles
articles.summary: This brief article, titled "Doubles," emphasizes that observing the movement of stars, particularly double stars, is a challenging task. It states that resolving such stellar motion serves as a significant test for powerful instruments, specifically mentioning 100-inch telescopes.

articles.title: RESOLVING POWER
articles.summary: This article explains Dawes' Limit, the accepted empirical resolution limit for visual telescopes, providing a table that correlates telescope aperture with the closest angular separation it can resolve. While originally defined for specific star conditions, it serves as a reliable predictor for excellent optics. The author also shares a personal definition of resolution and an example from their 10" Newtonian telescope.

articles.title: Election of Board Members
articles.summary: On February 6, 1993, the Association held its Board Member elections. The incumbent members were re-elected, and Jim Hodgers was elected to replace Steve Greenberg, who was recognized for his significant dedication and contributions. The article lists the names of the current board members.

articles.title: Special Star Parties
articles.summary: The article announces two upcoming "Special Star Parties" in March, detailing locations and times for events at Main School Alviso on March 2nd and Almaden Episcopal Church on March 31st. It provides specific directions and a contact number for more information, while also requesting increased member participation and more telescopes to handle potentially large crowds.

articles.title: E.T. Again
articles.summary: This article is a letter from Bill Dellinges, responding to a previous article about NGC 457, also known as the "Owl" or "Airplane" cluster. Bill shares observing tips for NGC 457 in Cassiopeia, detailing how to locate it and mentioning its various nicknames. He also recommends observing the triple star Iota Cassiopeia and the open cluster NGC 7789, sharing personal enjoyment and magnification tips for these objects.

articles.title: Star Parties - January '93
articles.summary: This report details various star parties held in January 1993, highlighting mixed success due to weather and logistical issues at Fremont Peak and Grant Ranch. Despite these challenges, successful and well-attended star parties took place at John Muir School and Houge Park, featuring multiple telescopes and celestial observations. The article also touches upon the use of club loaner telescopes and a technical issue with a diagonal mirror's adhesive.

articles.title: The Eye piece
articles.summary: This snippet from "The Eye piece" refers to an upcoming event or package requiring advance ticket reservations. Readers are encouraged to look for further details in future announcements published in Astronomy Magazine.

articles.title: Observing Sites
articles.summary: The article announces a new initiative to compile an updated booklet of local astronomy observing sites within an hour's drive, building upon previous efforts. Readers are encouraged to submit their suggestions for sites, including a map, description, and a reference person, to the editor.

articles.title: Observing Tools
articles.summary: This document proposes an article detailing personal observing tools and preparations for an astronomical observing session. It suggests listing essential items such as warm clothing, eyepieces, charged batteries, and star charts. The article also prompts discussion on effective packing and organization to easily locate items during an observing session.

articles.title: Astro Ads
articles.summary: This document features a series of classified advertisements for used astronomical equipment, including various telescopes and accessories from brands like Meade, Astro-Physics, and Celestron. It also provides the 1993 calendar of events for the San Jose Astronomical Association, outlining general meetings, star parties, and astronomy classes. Lastly, the article includes an update on the SJAA's telescope loaner program, listing currently borrowed instruments and their due dates.

articles.title: ASTRO ADS
articles.summary: This document outlines "ASTRO ADS," a free classifieds section for noncommercial advertisers to sell astronomically related products or services. It provides instructions for ad submission, including a monthly deadline and duration for ads. The content then lists several actual advertisements for various astronomical equipment, such as Newtonian and Classic C-8 telescopes, a Celestron 14, a Takahashi FC 125 refractor, and Orion astronomical binoculars, detailing their specifications and asking prices.

articles.title: March 1993
articles.summary: This document provides astronomical data for March 1993, detailing lunar phases, rise/set/transit times for the Sun and major planets (Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn), and their respective magnitudes and distances. It also includes astronomical twilight times, sidereal time, and highlights the 'Darkest Saturday Night' for observational purposes. All times and dates are given in Pacific Standard Time (PST) and credit multiple software and handbook sources for the data's derivation.

articles.title: Offices and Board of Directors
articles.summary: This document outlines the current offices and Board of Directors for an organization. It lists the names and phone numbers for key leadership positions including the President, Vice President, Treasurer, Secretary, and several Directors.

articles.title: Ephemeris Contributors
articles.summary: This document lists the names and phone numbers of individuals who contribute to an 'Ephemeris', as well as the editor responsible for it. It serves as a contact directory for those involved in the ephemeris's creation and publication.

articles.title: Comet comments
articles.summary: This article provides an update on several comets, highlighting Periodic Comet Schaumasse's current visibility in the northern evening sky. It details the recent discovery of Comet Mueller (1993a) in January by Jean Mueller, predicting it will reach magnitude 8 by January next year. The document also reports the recovery of Periodic Comet Bus (1993b) and Periodic Comet Tempel 1 (1993c) by Jim Scotti, noting their anticipated visibility for observers.

articles.title: PERIODIC COMET SCHAUMASSE (1992x)
articles.summary: This article provides an ephemeris for Periodic Comet Schaumasse (1992x) from February 22 to April 13, 1993. It details the comet's Right Ascension, Declination, elongation, sky visibility, and estimated magnitude, serving as a guide for observers. The data was published in 'EPHEMERIS' by the San Jose Astronomical Association.

articles.title: SAN JOSE ASTRONOMICAL ASSOCIATION MEMBERSHIP
articles.summary: This document is a membership application form for the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA), outlining different membership types and their respective fees, including options for 'Membership Only,' 'Membership/S&T,' and 'Junior' memberships. It provides instructions for submitting the form and payment, along with contact information for the treasurer and a general SJAA hotline. The document also includes details like the association's address and indicates it's a non-profit organization, dating back to March 1993.

articles.title: May 1st, 1993
articles.summary: This document is a notice for an event held on May 1st, 1993, at Houge Park in San Jose. The event featured a swap meet from 2:00 PM to 5:00 PM, followed by an auction at 6:00 PM, with doors opening at 1:00 PM.

articles.title: Astronomical goodies galore
articles.summary: This article serves as an announcement for an event where a wide variety of astronomical equipment and accessories are available. It lists everything from complete telescopes and optics to electronics, cameras, books, and miscellaneous items, encouraging readers to bring their own unused astronomy treasures.

articles.title: The San Jose Astronomical Association
articles.summary: This document introduces the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA), providing its name and primary location. The association is situated at Houge Park in San Jose, near Highway 17 and Camden Avenue, with a note that a map is available for further directional details.

articles.title: Directions to HOUGE PARK
articles.summary: This document provides directions to Houge Park, featuring a map with street names for navigation. It also includes a registration form for the 1993 Bay Area Astronomical Auction, detailing fields for bidder information, items, minimum bids, and a note that 10% of all sales will benefit the SJAA.
